From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Park <julie@veridian.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: End-to-end latency tradeoffs & tail targets — hosted migration recap

Julie — thanks again for the call today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Quick summary of Veridian asks (from the call)
- End-to-end SLO targets: 95th <= 250 ms, 99th <= 700 ms (interactive product path)
- Sustained throughput: ~120 req/s for the primary region (US-WEST) with occasional bursts to 300 req/s for 2–3 min
- Concurrency: up to 75 concurrent streaming sessions (server-streaming responses with partial tokens)
- Streaming constraints: client expects incremental tokens delivered within 60 ms of generation for each chunk; total end-to-end includes routing, pre/post-processing, network to/from our hosted API

Current provider baseline (from what you shared on-call): p95 ~430 ms, p99 ~1.2 s (end-to-end under your test harness).

What Redwood proposes next
- Action 1: We’ll run a controlled side-by-side using your sample traffic (you mentioned a CSV export) against our hosted API and the incumbent. Goal: mirror your real traffic envelope (burst windows + streaming pattern).
- Action 2: Share a lightweight test harness (client + traffic generator) by EOD Tuesday so you can run locally and we can self-run in-parallel.
- Action 3: Engineering deep-dive to confirm our streaming chunk latency (Logan + Naomi) — target to surface microsecond-level dispatch times and where tails originate.
- Action 4: Exchange artifact: Veridian provides a 1-hour p95/p99 trace (or summarized CSV) and we return an annotated timeline + bottleneck hypothesis.

Proposed schedule
- Tue 22 Jun: test harness + sample CSV shared (by Veridian)
- Wed 23 Jun: Redwood runs first-pass side-by-side test and shares raw metrics
- Fri 25 Jun: sync to review acceptance criteria and routing/fallback policies

Attachments: I’ve attached our draft SLO proposal (redwood_slo_proposal_v2.pdf) with recommended ingestion routing, prewarm window suggestions, and throttling/fallback knobs.

Immediate asks for you: 1) share the CSV/trace (veridian_latency_sample.csv), 2) confirm whether cold-starts matter for your production window, 3) confirm a demo window Wed 23 Jun 10:00–11:00 PT if that works.

Thanks — Kim

Kim — thanks for the fast recap and for putting the SLO doc up front. Confirming a few things and sharing the sample CSV (attached).

Notes from our side:
- We attached a 1-hour production sample (veridian_latency_sample.csv) extracted from yesterday’s traffic. It includes timestamps, region, client RTTs, and our current provider’s end-to-end timing per request.
- Current provider baseline in that CSV: p95 430 ms, p99 1.2 s (these are the end-to-end numbers that drove today’s lift-and-shift discussion).
- Cold-starts: we’ve historically seen a 150–300 ms spike on rare scale events; they’re painful during the first 30 minutes of a heavy roll. Would be great to understand your prewarm strategy.

We can do Wed 23 Jun 10:00 PT for the initial live run — Tom will join the demo and procurement is cc’d for timeline visibility.

One ask for your engineering team: when you run the side-by-side, can you also capture token-level generation latency and the time spent in our network vs compute? Even an annotated CSV with columns for (client_rtt, ingress_latency, model_compute, egress_latency) would be hugely helpful.

Thanks — Julie

Team — forwarding Julie’s CSV and our ask from the call. High-level engineering asks below; please triage and tell me which we can deliver by Wed 10:00 PT (demo time).

Quoted message below.

Action items for runtime/bench team (Logan + Naomi)
- A1: Run the side-by-side using Veridian CSV traffic as-is. Produce p50/p95/p99, and breakdown columns: ingress (LB) time, model compute, egresstime.
- A2: Streaming chunk latency: instrument the hosted path to capture per-chunk dispatch times and any queueing at batching layer. Target: capture percentiles up to 99.99.
- A3: Cold-start plan: outline prewarm window and expected impact on p95/p99 for a warm pool size of 10–20 concurrent sessions. Include recommended warm-up strategy for sudden burst windows.
- A4: Synthetic stress: run burst to 300 req/s for 3 minutes to observe tail behavior and document any fallback triggers (routing to variant models, graceful degradation).

When you reply to this thread, please paste: 1) a concise runbook for the Wed demo (what we will measure + what we will show live), and 2) the list of artifacts we will hand back to Veridian post-run (CSV + annotated timeline + candidate mitigations).

Thanks — Kim

Kim, team — quick follow-up from my side. Appreciated the call — two clarifications from product/procurement before the Wed demo.

1) Acceptance criteria we’ll use internally
- Phase 1 (proof): matched or improved p95 (<= 430 ms) and material reduction to p99 (target <= 850 ms). If hosted can hit your stated 95/99 targets (250/700) we’ll consider that an over-deliver and accelerate procurement.
- Phase 2 (SLA): sustained 120 req/s with no regressions in p99 over a 1-hour window during controlled traffic — otherwise discuss rolling throttle/fallback policies.

2) Workload notes — token lengths and streaming pattern
- Typical request size: 120–400 tokens; ~65% of sessions expect streaming partial tokens (chunk size ~32 tokens) until the end-of-stream event.
- Regional split: 85% US-WEST, 10% US-EAST, 5% APAC (we will run US-WEST first).

3) Procurement timeline & paperwork
- We’ve assigned an internal PM to accelerate sign-off. Procurement needs a target SOW and pricing estimate by Fri 25 Jun to meet our July renewal cycle. I’ve attached a placeholder DocuSign link for SOW review.

We’ll see you Wed 23 Jun 10:00 PT.

— Tom
